name: Finance
boundaries: Finance: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: Explaining major anomalies is a useful test, but a model with no free parameters and no exceptions is not imposed as a necessary condition.

original_dispositions.original_title: Predictive theory of crises and systemic risk
original_dispositions.reason: Probabilistic, intervention-specific prediction replaces the unsupported promise of predicting every crisis.

original_dispositions.original_title: Risk-free rate puzzle and safe-asset shortage
original_dispositions.reason: Not added separately. A credible general asset-pricing theory in FIN-01 should address safe-asset prices where relevant, but a complete theory of long-run rates and safe-asset supply is not claimed to have been solved by FIN-01. The historical entry states a major research question without specifying a distinct capability whose resolution alone clearly meets the requested impact threshold. In particular, an explanation would not automatically produce accurate long-term discount rates. “Are US Treasury Bonds Still a Safe Haven?” discusses convenience yields and competing forces; it does not establish one universal explanation: https://www.nber.org/reporter/2020number3/are-us-treasury-bonds-still-safe-haven?page=1&perPage=50.

This is a consequential problem, but the historical proposal does not identify a distinct demonstrated or sufficiently specified mechanism that would ensure universal, time-consistent restructuring while preserving market access. Collective-action clauses already address part of the holdout problem. The IMF’s 2025 stocktaking, p. 19, reports both their use in recent bond restructurings and substantial delays in a small set of cases; those observations do not imply that serial crises can be ended: https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/pp/2025/english/ppea2025034.pdf.
Added as FIN-08, with overlap with FIN-02.

original_dispositions.original_title: ESG and sustainable-finance pricing and impact
original_dispositions.reason: Added as FIN-09, with financial pricing and causal real-world additionality treated as separate questions.

original_dispositions.original_title: Endogenous money creation without run fragility
original_dispositions.reason: The practical run-resistant financing component is covered by FIN-03. A complete explanation of money creation and credit cycles is not claimed, and ending boom-bust cycles is not a demonstrated consequence.
FIN-01 permits adaptive and behavioral mechanisms without presuming that all apparent inefficiencies arise from one rational-agent explanation.

original_dispositions.original_title: Market financing of pure public goods
original_dispositions.reason: Added as FIN-10, subject to explicit incentive, budget and feasibility limits.

original_dispositions.original_title: Information-theoretic limit on predictability and arbitrage
original_dispositions.reason: Existing restricted bounds are acknowledged; a universal exact alpha limit is not assumed possible.

reconciliation_change_log.reason: Preserved their identities and central capabilities. Claims remain conditional on evidence and deployment; completion criteria are explicitly proposals.
The historical microstructure-to-crash concept has a distinct causal mechanism and market-design application, although it overlaps with systemic cascades in FIN-02.
The historical sustainable-finance idea is narrowed to causal, auditable measurement of both financial effects and real-world additionality; labels and scores alone do not qualify.
Public-goods financing is framed as a substantial practical mechanism with explicit incentive and budget trade-offs, rather than an assumed universal solution.
Information-theoretic limits are retained as a distinct mathematical capability, while acknowledging that important bounds already exist in restricted settings.

reconciliation_change_log.change: The historical list’s promises to predict every crisis, end credit cycles, eliminate bailouts or solve planetary free riding are not treated as established consequences.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The research notes do not establish those consequences.
